verification: Combination rule (driver :354-362): PASS iff C1 or C2, PASS -> supports. This was pre-registered and reasoned in the driver docstring, so the misread is not a hidden driver defect; it is in what 'supports SD-011' was taken to mean.

C1 is worse than 'chance-level discrimination' at the level of the raw-norm MEAN: damage-sourced z_harm_a mean norm is seed-determined and density-invariant (spread std 7e-5 across 0-8 hazards). Red-team qualification: MECH-303's 2026-08-16 V3-EXQ-930 note records within-seed std rising monotonically with density (9.8e-04 -> 2.1e-03), so the output is not wholly environment-blind -- an ABSOLUTE threshold on the raw norm cannot discriminate at this seed offset; a per-seed standardised read might.

The prior confirmed autopsy's supports rationale -- 'damage-sourced z_harm_a tracks accumulated homeostatic deviation, its SD-011 job, and is therefore the wrong signal for MECH-303' -- is not shown by this run: a density-invariant output is not shown to track accumulated damage either. Both sourcing modes feed the same z_harm_a stream (two untrained AffectiveHarmEncoder instances, 7-dim and 50-dim input), so the run compares two INPUTS to one stream; it never compares z_harm_s with z_harm_a, which is what SD-011's separation asserts.

Not previously applied to the SD-011 disposition (MECH-303's 2026-08-16 V3-EXQ-930 note already records the untrained encoder and its ~60x init-offset-to-modulation ratio; surfaced here by the Step 7b C2 fire on sd_zharm_a_warmup_optimizer_group): the 917 driver has no optimizer and no training loop -- the AffectiveHarmEncoder is an UNTRAINED random projection in both modes. Damage-sourced input is 7-dim limb damage with heal_rate 0.4 (near zero on most ticks of a 150-tick random walk); proximity input is a 50-dim EMA of the hazard/resource fields, which varies with density. C2 PASS therefore shows that a random projection of a density-varying input varies with density, and C1's seed-determined output is the random init read through a near-constant input. That entry (p0h stage BUILT 2026-09-19) is the route for giving z_harm_a a trained path.

The driver's own grid makes either outcome non-discriminating for SD-011: C2 PASS shows the AffectiveHarmEncoder can transmit a proximity input (an encoder-transmission positive control); the FAIL branch would have shown an encoder that destroys its input (an implementation defect). Neither bears on the design decision to split the stream. Precedent: failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-472_2026-09-02 recorded an unscored SD-011 calibration pilot non_contributory on the same grounds.
